clue.text: Imposed as a duty on the vicar, for example

definitions.meaning: a duty that is binding upon someone rests on them as an obligation
a vicar holding a parish benefice is the current holder of that office

explanation.surface: A duty laid upon the parish vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: an adjective meaning resting on someone as an obligation, and a noun for the holder of a church living.

clue.text: Example of man in nice predicament

indicators.note: the man's name sits inside the shuffled letters of the next word
a predicament is a mess, so the letters of nice are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Stan is a man's name

explanation.surface: An example of a man stuck in a nice predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predicament' looks like the situation the man is in, but it is the signal that nice is to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited as an example, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Pass one about to have stomach trouble

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
the Roman numeral for one is I
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing a mountain pass is about to suffer stomach pains.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, a form of stomach trouble.

clue.text: Plan dramatist rushes for London Zoo feature

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
Harold Pinter was an English dramatist
races means rushes, hurries

explanation.surface: A playwright hurriedly draws up a plan for a feature at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mappin Terraces are an artificial mountain landscape built at London Zoo in 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mappin Terraces are a famous terraced enclosure at London Zoo, a specific example of its features.

clue.text: Oriental birdman goes on and on

parts.note: E for East, so Oriental
the word splits into a seabird, the tern, followed by the man's name Al

explanation.surface: An eastern bird-fancier who never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birdman' reads as one word, an aviator, but must be split into a bird and a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal describes something without end, so a phrase meaning lasting forever fits it.

clue.text: Toy with coy Greek ruler

parts.note: a spinning top is a toy
arch means playfully sly or coy

explanation.surface: A ruler in Greece playing coyly with a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A toparch was a ruler of a small district or state in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Fresh pair of horses

definitions.meaning: neat and new, as in the phrase spick and ...
a matched team of two horses harnessed together

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: an old word for clean and new, and an American term for a pair of draught animals.

clue.text: Some spruce old actor longs to be out

indicators.note: the yearning word is to be on the outside, wrapped around the performer

parts.note: pines means longs, yearns
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A dapper veteran actor longs to get out of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some spruce' looks like 'rather smart', but spruce is the tree; Tree was an actor famed on the Edwardian London stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruces belong to the pine family, so a group of spruces can be called conifers of that kind.

clue.text: Limited contract

definitions.meaning: to become tighter or thinner, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: an adjective meaning restricted and a verb meaning to make or become thinner.

clue.text: Fruit of Chinese royal dynasty

parts.note: Mandarin is the main Chinese language
the House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A fruit associated with a Chinese royal dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Orange gave England William III.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin orange is a small citrus fruit, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Fool getting look-in in Shropshire

indicators.note: the word for look goes inside the word for fool

parts.note: a sap is a fool
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A fool gets a look-in somewhere in Shropshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look-in' splits into look (LO) and the container signal in.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the traditional abbreviated name of the English county of Shropshire.

clue.text: He makes clear letter clearer

parts.note: ex is the spelt-out name of the letter X
plainer means clearer

explanation.surface: A man who explains things writes a letter clearer than most.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who explains things is one who makes them clear, so the phrase describes him.

clue.text: Bridge for sale

definitions.meaning: ... bridge, a form of the card game
put up to be sold to the highest bidder

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a variety of the card game bridge, and a public sale where goods go to the top bidder.

clue.text: Free to go back to old dance party

parts.note: rid means free

indicators.note: the first to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Free to return to a dance from times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns the first TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridotto was an eighteenth-century social gathering with music and dancing, often masked.

clue.text: Grave accusation constituting an attack on most important city

definitions.meaning: an accusation of a crime punishable by death

definitions.text: an attack on most important city
definitions.meaning: a charge as a military assault on the chief city

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: an indictment for a crime carrying the death penalty, and literally an assault upon a capital city.

clue.text: Reaching sexual maturity to find local scene changing at last

parts.note: a local is a pub, a neighbourhood bar

indicators.note: the letters of scene are changing their order
only the final letter of at is used

explanation.surface: Teenagers find the scene at the local changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges SCENE to ESCEN; 'last' takes T from 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubescent describes someone at the stage of puberty, becoming capable of reproduction.

clue.text: Press seaman for symbol of firmness

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
a hand is a crew member on a ship

explanation.surface: Navy recruiters press a sailor into service as a show of strength.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron hand is an idiom for strict, unyielding control.

clue.text: Natural storage container for a first-class manager

parts.note: born means natural, innate
an organiser is a box or rack for keeping things tidy

explanation.surface: A natural storage box made for an excellent manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is a natural at organising people is an excellent administrator.

clue.text: Scare's about a wicked Englishman, initially

definitions.note: the definition is the verb scare, with 's as a link meaning is

parts.note: over can mean about, concerning

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words are used

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened by a wicked Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes W and E from 'wicked Englishman'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to intimidate, filling someone with fear or awe.

clue.text: Virtuous urge that's lucky!

parts.note: good means virtuous
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A virtuous impulse turns out to be fortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good egg!' is a dated British exclamation of delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The old exclamation was used to welcome good news, just like saying what a stroke of luck.

clue.text: Revolutionary ways to make strong boxes

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary
St is the abbreviation for street, a way, so ways gives STS

explanation.surface: Revolutionary methods for making strongboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chests are sturdy boxes for storing valuables.

clue.text: Human pledge to put label in stockings

indicators.note: the label goes inside the stockings

parts.note: hose are stockings
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A promise to sew name labels into one's stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held as security for a promise, a living pledge.

clue.text: Athlete regularly involved in rows

definitions.meaning: someone who often takes part in rowing, read as quarrelling

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a sportsperson, and someone who habitually rows a boat, disguised as being always in arguments.

clue.text: Happy chance to show clemency

definitions.meaning: a fortunate event, as in it is a blessing that
forgiveness or leniency shown to someone

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a stroke of luck, as in it's a blessing, and compassion shown to an offender.

clue.text: Smooth story about town

indicators.note: the word for story goes around the word for smooth

parts.note: a stage is a level or storey of a building, spelt story in American English
even means smooth, level

explanation.surface: A smooth tale about a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Story here is a floor of a building, not a tale. Stevenage is a new town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is an English town in Hertfordshire, an example of the general term.

clue.text: The girl from Standard One

parts.note: a norm is a standard
a means one

explanation.surface: A girl from Standard One at primary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a girl's name, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Fixed soundly to provide home for animal

indicators.note: soundly signals that a word is said, not spelt

parts.note: set means fixed

explanation.surface: Something firmly fixed provides a home for a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the burrow of a badger, a home for an animal.

clue.text: Bird observed by the keen of sight

parts.note: the eagle is a bird
eyed means observed

explanation.surface: A bird watched by sharp-sighted spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagle-eyed means having very sharp vision, as eagles do.
